« J’ai grandi à Saint-Michel et la raiso: “I grew up in Saint-Michel, and the reason I wanted to open a salon here is the sense of belonging.”
À l’angle du boulevard Saint-Michel et d: At the corner of Saint-Michel Boulevard and Émile-Journault Street, just behind the 67 bus stop, stands the salon’s storefront. Through the windows, you can see employees coming and going, and clients getting pampered. Push open the door and you’re swept up in a soundtrack of 1990s hip-hop and bachata. The salon’s name, Pretty Little Thing, is written in neon pink on the black wall above the open space where the hairstylists and nail technicians work. At the front of the shop, a woman is getting her nails done, and beside her, a child plays with a baby in a stroller. A little further along, a hairstylist and her client are swapping stories about their day. Seated in a director’s chair facing the camera, the young entrepreneur shares her journey in the hope of inspiring people like her to push beyond their limits.
« Je viens d’une famille pauvre […], mai: “I come from a poor family […], but just because you don’t come from a rich family doesn’t mean you can’t succeed. You choose your destiny, and you just have to not give up,” says the young woman.
Ngan Julie Trinh gère deux entreprises e: Ngan Julie Trinh runs two businesses in addition to her salon, as well as the Académie Pretty Little Thing. Because of her path, she is a source of inspiration for the young women in her neighbourhood. “The fact that she was an entrepreneur so young inspires me a lot,” says Arleen Cristal, 18, who works at the salon and trained at the Académie PLT.
Âgée de 29 ans, Julie possède déjà un ri: At 29, Julie already has a rich track record in the world of entrepreneurship. At 24, she opened her first business, a banh mi restaurant, with her partner. It hasn’t always been smooth sailing for this go-getter. When they launched that first project, La Viet Sandwicherie, Julie and her partner put in all their savings. At the time, the young woman had to juggle numerous responsibilities to keep her business running and make a living. “In the morning, I would get up and go to work at the bank. After that, I would go to the restaurant, and then I had evening classes at university. When classes ended, I worked at a bar until 4 a.m.,” she says. The salon owner kept up that pace for two years. Despite the ups and downs, Julie managed to get back on her feet and, above all, learn from her mistakes. After selling the restaurant, she is now getting ready to open another business.
Julie revient sur son enfance et sa fami: Julie looks back on her childhood and her family, which are a major source of motivation for her. She has made her past her own and turned it into a strength. Life hasn’t always been easy, but that is what inspires the clients, students and employees who are going through situations similar to what she lived through a few years ago. “I haven’t been talking about it for very long; I’m a private person,” she says. “Now, when I hear people tell me that their family has money problems and that they have to work to help their parents, I can tell them I went through the same thing.” Watching her mother hold four jobs at once, Julie wanted to succeed so she could give her a better quality of life. “Unfortunately, our parents come here and live to work. I really wanted them to live,” she adds, speaking over the cries of a child visiting the salon. That is her greatest accomplishment: making her mother proud and giving her the chance to quit three of her jobs and keep just one.
Depuis son ouverture, il y a trois ans,: Since it opened three years ago, the salon has built up a loyal clientele. That is the case for Lorie, who is a regular at PLT. Today, her relationship with the owner goes beyond a simple professional one. “Sometimes we go out to eat together,” says Lorie of their friendship. She says that going to PLT not only gets her beauty services, it is also “a way to support Julie, a young person like us who made it.” And it’s about more than her friend’s success. “She inspires the young people in the neighbourhood, for whom it’s hard to succeed; she creates jobs and brings change and courage.”
Ouvrir une entreprise dans Saint-Michel: Opening a business in Saint-Michel was a no-brainer for Julie. She grew up on Pie-IX Boulevard in a Vietnamese family and spent her entire youth in this neighbourhood.
Naturellement, lorsque l’idée de lancer: Naturally, when the idea of launching another business took hold, she saw it as the ideal location. Julie doesn’t let herself be distracted by the narratives that sometimes paint the neighbourhood in a negative light. “A lot of people think that because you set up in Saint-Michel, it won’t work,” she laments.
Forte de son expérience en gestion de co: Drawing on her experience in business management and marketing, she was able to identify the advantages her neighbourhood offers. “I did a lot of calculations. […] First of all, I’m on Saint-Michel Boulevard, which is a very busy artery and is right next to Highway 40. We’re close to a bus stop and several high schools,” she lists.
Le salon est aussi le cheval de bataille: The salon is also Ngan Julie’s cause and allows her to break down many of the stereotypes associated with the neighbourhood. “Just because you come from a more disadvantaged place doesn’t mean you’re not professional,” she says, pointing out that local businesses offer service and management as good as those set up elsewhere. “We can also create jobs for the people around us,” the entrepreneur adds.
Julie compte actuellement 26 employés. P: Julie currently has 26 employees. Among them is Arleen Cristal. “I’ve known Julie since I was 14. I used to come here with my mother to get my nails done. She watched me grow up,” the student says shyly. The young woman tells us that she started her career as an aesthetician at the salon on a whim. “I was getting a treatment when I heard Julie talking about the Académie PLT. I thought, ‘Why not give it a try?’” she explains.
Un an plus tard, Arleen est devenue esth: A year later, Arleen became an aesthetician at the salon. Working at Pretty Little Thing allowed her to overcome her shyness and become more outgoing. Under her mentor’s wing, Arleen also caught the entrepreneurial bug. She plans to continue her studies in business management and open her own business soon. “I’m very interested in the restaurant industry and in the idea of starting a business,” she says.
« Peu importe ton passé, tu peux toujour: “No matter your past, you can always succeed” – that is the message Julie has for the youth of Saint-Michel.
